title: RUNBOOK (DRAFT): Dedicated staged rollouts — Gate failures / paused rollouts triage
content:
NOTE: This is a working draft for dogfood + early beta. Expect churn as evaluator + routing behavior evolves.

Last reviewed: 2025-02-19 (after evaluator lag incident / dogfood).
Primary oncall: SRE (Dedicated/Inference Platform). Secondary: Eng Platform (Control plane), Eng Infra (Dedicated fleet), Observability.

============================================================
1) Purpose / scope
============================================================
This runbook covers triage and response when a Dedicated staged rollout is:
- Paused / held due to a failing gate
- Paused due to missing/late metrics (fail-safe)
- Stuck (not advancing) due to evaluator degradation or approval issues
- Causing customer-visible impact during stage transitions (queue depth, latency, 5xx)

This runbook assumes v1 behavior:
- Deterministic traffic allocation by stage weights
- Gates evaluated server-side by gate evaluator service
- Fail-safe: missing metrics or evaluator degradation => HOLD (do not advance)
- Manual approvals may be required between stages (policy-dependent)

Out of scope (for now): complex A/B experimentation (handled separately).

============================================================
2) Definitions (quick)
============================================================
- Pool: Dedicated reserved GPU pool. pool_id is the primary unit of isolation.
- Rollout plan: versioned object containing stages + gates + approval policy.
- Stage: traffic weight + evaluation window + gates + optional manual approval.
- Gate: condition evaluated on metrics over a window. Gate can be PASS / FAIL / NO_DATA.
- HOLD: rollout is paused. No further automatic stage progression.
- ABORT: stop rollout; routing returns to previous stable target (or configured fallback).

============================================================
3) Severity guidance (S0/S1/S2) — DRAFT
============================================================
S0 (page): Customer production outage or sustained severe latency; dedicated pool saturated; elevated 5xx/timeouts; cannot serve traffic within SLA.
S1 (page): Material degradation (p95 latency above SLA threshold, queue depth rising) but partial service; rollout still proceeding or stuck in risky state.
S2 (ticket / async): Rollout paused with no customer impact; evaluator NO_DATA holds; approvals confusion; console mismatch.

============================================================
4) Fast path: 5-minute triage checklist
============================================================
Input required: tenant, pool_id, rollout_plan_id, current_stage.

[ ] Confirm whether customer impact exists (latency, errors, timeouts).
[ ] Identify cause category:
    (A) Real regression / capacity issue
    (B) Metrics pipeline lag / missing metrics (false hold)
    (C) Gate evaluator degraded (late ticks, errors)
    (D) Approval/RBAC/state machine issue
    (E) Console display bug (backend truth differs)

[ ] If customer impact is ongoing: ABORT rollout first, then investigate.
[ ] If no customer impact: prefer HOLD while investigating; do not “force advance” unless metrics freshness is verified.

============================================================
5) Step-by-step decision flowcharts (ASCII)
============================================================

5.1) High-level flow

+--------------------------------------------------+
| Rollout is PAUSED / customer reports rollout issue|
+--------------------------+-----------------------+
                           |
                           v
                +----------------------+     +------------------------+
                | Any customer impact? |--Y->| Mitigate FIRST: ABORT, |
                +----------+-----------+     | reduce traffic weight, |
                           |                 | scale/guardrails check |
                           N                 +-----------+------------+
                           |                             |
                           v                             v
              +-----------------------+        +------------------------+
              | Gate reason / message |        | After mitigation: find |
              | FAIL vs NO_DATA?      |        | root cause + followups |
              +-----------+-----------+        +------------------------+
                          |
          +---------------+----------------+
          |                                |
          v                                v
+---------------------+        +------------------------------+
| FAIL (has data)     |        | NO_DATA / METRICS_MISSING    |
| => likely real issue|        | => freshness / pipeline check|
+----------+----------+        +---------------+--------------+
           |                                   |
           v                                   v
+---------------------+         +------------------------------+
| Capacity vs regression? |     | Metrics pipeline healthy?    |
| queue depth/util vs code |     | evaluator healthy?          |
+----------+----------+         +---------------+--------------+
           |                                   |
           v                                   v
   +---------------+                 +-------------------------+
   | ABORT/ROLLBACK |                 | If pipeline issue: HOLD |
   | and file bug   |                 | + engage Observability  |
   +---------------+                 +-------------------------+


5.2) “Should I abort?” flow (biased toward safety)

+-----------------------------+
| Are we past Stage 0/1?      |
| (>= 25% traffic)            |
+--------------+--------------+
               |
               v
     +-------------------+
     | Customer impact?  |
     +----+---------+----+
          |         |
          Y         N
          |         |
          v         v
+----------------+  +-------------------------------+
| ABORT NOW      |  | Is gate FAIL with strong      |
| (stop the line)|  | signal? (errors/latency)      |
+----------------+  +-----------+-------------------+
                               |
                               v
                     +--------------------+
                     | If uncertain: HOLD |
                     | until metrics fresh|
                     +--------------------+

============================================================
6) Where to look (dashboards / logs / tooling)
============================================================

6.1) Dashboards (Grafana)
- Dedicated Rollout Overview (per pool)
  https://grafana.redwoodinference.internal/d/ded-rollout-overview
  Panels:
   - Current stage + traffic weights (control plane)
   - Gate outcomes (PASS/FAIL/NO_DATA)
   - Evaluator tick lag + error rate
   - p50/p95/p99 latency (end-to-end + model)
   - 5xx + timeout rate
   - Queue depth + queue wait time
   - GPU utilization + memory

- Gate Evaluator Health
  https://grafana.redwoodinference.internal/d/ded-rollout-evaluator-health
  Panels:
   - evaluations/sec by region
   - evaluation duration p95
   - last_success_timestamp skew
   - NO_DATA rate by metric

- Dedicated Pool Capacity / Autoscaling
  https://grafana.redwoodinference.internal/d/dedicated-pool-capacity
  Panels:
   - headroom (% idle GPU)
   - autoscaler actions / blocks (min headroom guardrail)
   - saturation signals

6.2) Logs
- Gate evaluator service: rollout-gate-evaluator
  - Kibana: https://logs.redwoodinference.internal/app/discover (index: prod-rollout-evaluator-*)
  - Filter hints:
    service=rollout-gate-evaluator
    pool_id=<pool_id>
    rollout_plan_id=<plan_id>
    error_code in (METRICS_TIMEOUT, QUERY_ERROR, WINDOW_INCOMPLETE)

- Control plane API service: rollout-control-plane
  - Look for optimistic concurrency / version mismatch / approval events.

6.3) Internal CLI (rw-admin) — DRAFT NAMES
- Get rollout status:
  rw-admin dedicated rollouts get --pool <pool_id>

- List audit events:
  rw-admin dedicated rollouts events list --pool <pool_id> --limit 200

- Abort rollout:
  rw-admin dedicated rollouts abort --pool <pool_id> --reason "SRE abort: gate failure + customer impact"

- Hold rollout (if not already held):
  rw-admin dedicated rollouts hold --pool <pool_id> --reason "Investigating metrics freshness"

- Approve stage (ONLY if policy allows and you’ve validated metrics freshness):
  rw-admin dedicated rollouts approve-stage --pool <pool_id> --stage <stage_id> --reason "SRE approve after validation"

============================================================
7) Common scenarios + playbooks
============================================================

7.1) Scenario A — Gate FAIL due to latency regression (p95)
Symptoms:
- Gate shows FAIL on latency p95 or timeout rate
- Customer reports slow requests / timeouts
- Queue depth may rise secondarily

Actions:
1) If impact > 5 minutes or violates SLA: ABORT rollout.
2) Confirm routing weight dropped back to stable target (watch Dedicated Rollout Overview).
3) Snapshot evidence:
   - current stage, stage weight, gate threshold, evaluation window
   - latency graphs before/after stage change
   - error/timeouts
4) Determine likely cause:
   - model change (new model version)
   - runtime flag/config change
   - kernel/quantization profile change
   - routing change / fallback behavior
5) Engage owners:
   - Routing: Mina Haddad / Ravi Menon
   - Control plane: Ethan Park
   - Runtime change: Serving runtime oncall (if applicable)
6) File incident follow-up:
   - Link plan_version and any correlated deploy/PR.

Notes:
- Watch for “p95 looks fine but queue wait explodes” -> treat as capacity/queue depth scenario.


7.2) Scenario B — Gate FAIL due to 5xx spikes
Symptoms:
- 5xx gate FAIL; error budget burn
- Potentially elevated request failures only for new stage target

Actions:
1) ABORT rollout (fastest mitigation).
2) Validate whether failure is concentrated on canary target pods/nodes.
3) Check recent deploys/flags for data plane (inference runtime) and routing layer.
4) If failures persist after abort:
   - This is no longer rollout-induced; treat as pool incident (Dedicated runbook: pool instability).


7.3) Scenario C — Gate FAIL due to queue depth / utilization (capacity)
Symptoms:
- Queue depth or queue wait time gate FAIL
- GPU util pinned; latency increases; throughput clamps
- Often occurs after moving from low traffic stage to >=25%

Actions:
1) If impact: ABORT rollout.
2) Check autoscaling guardrails dashboard:
   - Are we blocked by min headroom policy?
   - Is the pool at max reserved capacity?
3) Identify whether stage weight increase pushed pool beyond safe headroom.
4) If pool has no headroom (reserved):
   - Consider lowering rollout stage weight (if supported) OR abort.
   - Coordinate with Infra (Keiko Yamamoto / Vanessa Ortiz) if temporary burst capacity exists.
5) If headroom exists but queue is high:
   - suspect performance regression (model/runtime config) rather than pure capacity.

Preventive note:
- For Dedicated reserved pools, partial rollouts reduce effective capacity because some traffic is constrained to a subset of targets. Expect utilization artifacts at intermediate weights. This is why queue depth gates are mandatory.


7.4) Scenario D — Rollout held due to NO_DATA / missing metrics
Symptoms:
- Gate status: NO_DATA
- Hold reason: METRICS_MISSING / METRICS_LATE
- Dashboard shows evaluator NO_DATA rate spiking

Actions:
1) Do NOT force-advance. HOLD is correct behavior until freshness is verified.
2) Validate metrics freshness:
   - In Gate Evaluator Health dashboard: last_success_timestamp skew
   - In Dedicated Rollout Overview: “metrics age” panel if present
3) Check if issue is isolated (single pool/tenant) vs global.
4) If global metrics ingestion issue: page Observability oncall (Logan Wright / Caleb Johnson).
5) If isolated:
   - Check metric label cardinality drop / missing dimension (pool_id)
   - Validate pool exporter health (node/agent) and permissions
6) Temporary workaround (only if approved by SRE lead):
   - Extend evaluation window and re-evaluate (preferred)
   - Replace gate metric with a fallback metric (rare; risk of “metrics lie”)

If customer is waiting:
- Communicate “rollout safely paused due to missing telemetry; no traffic increase will occur until telemetry is reliable.”


7.5) Scenario E — Evaluator degraded / lag (late tick)
Symptoms:
- Evaluator tick lag panel shows increasing lag
- Rollouts not advancing / stuck in “evaluating”
- Potentially delayed HOLD when metrics are bad (this is worst-case)

Actions:
1) Treat as safety risk: ensure all active Dedicated rollouts are held.
   - Confirm global fail-safe is engaged (see PR_28572 behavior).
2) If fail-safe did NOT trigger and rollouts are advancing: escalate immediately to Eng Platform.
3) Inspect evaluator logs for:
   - query timeouts
   - backlog growth
   - downstream metrics store latency
4) If metrics backend is the bottleneck: engage Observability.
5) If evaluator CPU/memory exhausted: scale evaluator (per oncall procedure) and file follow-up.


7.6) Scenario F — Approval / RBAC / state machine weirdness
Symptoms:
- Console says “Waiting for approval” but approval click fails
- Approvals arrive concurrently and stage advancement races
- Stage shows inconsistent status between console and API

Actions:
1) Use source of truth: control plane status via rw-admin.
2) Pull audit event list for pool and confirm:
   - who attempted approval
   - what role / permission denied
   - which plan_version
3) If stuck due to version conflict:
   - Do not “edit plan” while trying to approve; reconcile to latest version first.
4) Engage:
   - Auth/RBAC: Kaitlyn Nguyen
   - Control plane: Ethan Park / Benji Okafor
   - Console backend: Chloe Martin

============================================================
8) Rollback/abort guidance (operator policy)
============================================================
Preferred ordering:
1) ABORT if customer impact or strong signal of regression.
2) HOLD if unclear signal, missing metrics, or investigating.
3) APPROVE/ADVANCE only when:
   - metrics freshness verified
   - gates stable for full evaluation window
   - headroom guardrail satisfied
   - stakeholder sign-off if required (policy)

What ABORT does (expected):
- Stops stage advancement
- Routing weight returns to previous stable target (or configured stable baseline)
- Emits audit event: rollout.abort

What HOLD does:
- Freezes stage advancement; routing stays at current stage weight
- Emits audit event: rollout.hold (manual) OR rollout.auto_hold (system)

============================================================
9) Communication templates (copy/paste)
============================================================

9.1) Internal (Slack #incidents or #eng-sre)
Title: Dedicated rollout paused/aborted — <tenant> / <pool_id>

Message:
- Summary: Paused/aborted Dedicated staged rollout for <tenant> pool <pool_id> due to <gate_name> (<FAIL|NO_DATA>). <customer impact yes/no>.
- Current status: <HOLD|ABORT> at stage <stage_id> (weight <x%>), plan <rollout_plan_id> v<plan_version>.
- Impact: <latency p95>, <5xx>, <queue depth> (include time range).
- Mitigation: <aborted at hh:mm>, routing reverted to <stable target>.
- Next steps: Investigating <metrics freshness|regression|capacity>. Engaging <names/teams>.
- Links:
  - Rollout overview dashboard: <grafana link>
  - Evaluator health dashboard: <grafana link>
  - Audit events: <if available>


9.2) Customer-facing (CS email draft)
Subject: Update: Dedicated model rollout paused for safety (no further traffic increase)

Body:
Hi <Name>,

We paused the staged rollout for your Dedicated pool (<pool_id>) after our automated safety gates detected <issue: elevated latency/queue depth/errors OR missing telemetry> during the <stage x%> phase.

What this means:
- The rollout will not progress to higher traffic percentages until we complete validation.
- We have <aborted the rollout and reverted traffic to the prior stable configuration / held the rollout at the current stage>.

Current observations (UTC):
- <p95 latency>: <value> (baseline: <value>)
- <error rate>: <value>
- <queue depth>: <value>

Next steps:
- We are investigating <root cause area> and will update you by <time>.
- If you can share any correlated application-side telemetry around <time window>, it may help.

Best,
<Oncall/SRE name> (via Redwood Support)


9.3) Status page / incident brief (internal)
- Customer: <tenant>
- Pool: <pool_id>
- Start time: <UTC>
- Detected by: gate <name>
- Mitigation: abort/hold
- Current: stable / monitoring

============================================================
10) Evidence to capture (for postmortem / bug)
============================================================
- rollout_plan_id + plan_version
- stage_id + intended weights
- gate_name + threshold + evaluation window
- evaluator tick lag at time of incident
- metrics timestamps (freshness) for each gate metric
- routing config snapshot (if available)
- audit events (create/update/approve/auto_hold/abort)
- links to relevant PRs / deploy ids

============================================================
11) Open questions / TODOs (keep this honest)
============================================================

- Add “reduce stage weight” procedure if supported (today we mostly have HOLD/ABORT).
- Clarify: when ABORT triggers automatic rollback vs stays pinned to stable target.
- Add explicit “metrics freshness contract” table (max metric age allowed per gate).
- Add quick links to per-region dashboards once URL paths finalize.
- Add section for “Console mismatch” known issues (INT-1120 class).
